title: The Global Economy
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Entender la macroeconomía es lo que diferencia a un gerente de un líder global. Conceptos como 'Inflation', 'Quantitative Easing' o distinguir un 'Bear Market' de un 'Bull Market' te permiten leer el mundo y anticipar el futuro.

parts.visual:
1. Inflation / Deflation (Inflación / Deflación): 
- Inflación: Aumento general de los precios y caída del poder adquisitivo. 
- Deflación: Caída general de los precios. 
Ej: Rampant INFLATION is destroying the middle class's purchasing power. 

2. Interest rates (Tasas de interés): 
- El costo de pedir dinero prestado. 
Ej: The central bank raised INTEREST RATES to combat inflation. 

3. Quantitative Easing (Expansión cuantitativa): 
- Cuando un banco central compra activos financieros para inyectar dinero en la economía. 
Ej: The government announced a new round of QUANTITATIVE EASING.
parts.audio: Welcome to The Global Economy and Macroeconomics. Number 1: Inflation and Deflation. Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money. Deflation is a decrease in prices. For example: Rampant INFLATION is destroying the middle class's purchasing power. Number 2: Interest rates. This is the cost of borrowing money. For example: The central bank raised INTEREST RATES to combat inflation. Number 3: Quantitative Easing. This happens when a central bank buys financial assets to inject money into the economy. For example: The government announced a new round of QUANTITATIVE EASING.

parts.visual:
4. Bear Market vs Bull Market: 
- Bear Market (Mercado bajista): Mercado donde los precios de las acciones caen. 
- Bull Market (Mercado alcista): Mercado donde los precios suben. 
Ej: We have been in a BULL MARKET for the past five years. 

5. Supply chain (Cadena de suministro): 
- La red de individuos, empresas, recursos y tecnología involucrados en la creación y venta de un producto. 
Ej: The pandemic caused massive GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN disruptions. 

6. GDP - Gross Domestic Product (PIB - Producto Interno Bruto): 
- El valor total de los bienes producidos y servicios prestados en un país durante un año. 
Ej: The country's GDP grew by 3% this quarter.
parts.audio: Number 4: Bear Market versus Bull Market. A Bear Market is when stock prices are falling. A Bull Market is when prices are rising. For example: We have been in a BULL MARKET for the past five years. Number 5: Supply chain. The network involved in the creation and sale of a product. For example: The pandemic caused massive GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAIN disruptions. Number 6: GDP, which stands for Gross Domestic Product. The total value of goods produced and services provided in a country. For example: The country's GDP grew by 3 percent this quarter.

questions.question: The central bank decided to lower ____ rates to encourage people to borrow and spend money. (Tasas de interés).
High ____ means your money buys less today than it did yesterday. (Inflación).
A stock market characterized by falling prices and pessimism is a ____ market.
questions.explanation: Bear market = mercado bajista (el oso ataca hacia abajo).

questions.question: A stock market characterized by rising prices and optimism is a ____ market.
questions.explanation: Bull market = mercado alcista (el toro ataca hacia arriba).

questions.question: The total value of goods and services produced by a country in one year is its Gross ____ Product (GDP).
questions.explanation: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) = Producto Interno Bruto (PIB).

questions.question: The global ____ chain was severely disrupted, causing shortages of microchips worldwide. (Cadena de suministro).
When a central bank creates money to buy government bonds and inject liquidity, it's called Quantitative ____.
A prolonged period of economic decline, typically defined as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth, is a ____.
A severe and prolonged downturn in economic activity is known as an economic ____.
questions.explanation: Depression = depresión económica (más grave y larga que una recesión).

questions.question: The amount of goods and services that a unit of currency can buy is its ____ power.
The difference in value between a country's imports and exports is its balance of ____.
Taxes imposed on imported goods and services are called ____. (Aranceles).
When the government spends more money than it takes in from taxes, it creates a budget ____. (Déficit).
When inflation is high, economic growth rate slows, and unemployment remains steadily high, the economy experiences ____.
The total amount of money that a country's government has borrowed is the national ____.
A financial ____ occurs when the price of an asset, like housing, rises far above its actual value and then suddenly drops.
A basic physical asset that is interchangeable with other goods of the same type (like oil, gold, or wheat) is a ____.
A tax levied on the purchase of goods and services is known as Value-____ Tax (VAT).
questions.explanation: Value-Added Tax (VAT) = Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA).

questions.question: The bank that provides financial and banking services for a country's government and commercial banking system is the ____ bank.
questions.explanation: Central bank = banco central (ej: la Reserva Federal).

questions.question: If inflation gets completely out of control, causing prices to rise extremely rapidly, it is called ____. (Hiperinflación).
High ____. (Inflación con I)
____ rates. (Tasas de interés con I)
A ____ market. (Mercado bajista con B)
A ____ market. (Mercado alcista con B)
Gross Domestic ____. (Producto Interno Bruto con P)
Global ____ chain. (Cadena de suministro con S)
Quantitative ____. (Expansión cuantitativa con E)
Economic ____. (Recesión con R)
Budget ____. (Déficit con D)
A housing ____. (Burbuja inmobiliaria con B)
